issues.legal_issue: A constitutional writ challenging statutory provisions becomes infructuous when the challenged provisions have been repealed.
material_facts: The landlords filed a writ petition challenging the constitutional validity of a rent-control statute and a provision requiring prior permission before eviction.
The statute was repealed while the petition was pending.

The landlords argued that orders made under the repealed statute remained in force and might obstruct relief under the new law; the court noted that they could seek relief under the new law if new circumstances had arisen.
issues.conclusion: The writ petition was dismissed as infructuous, with the parties bearing their own costs.
issues.legal_principle: The court treated repeal of the challenged statutory provisions as making the constitutional challenge infructuous. It did not decide the constitutional claims. It observed that relief could be sought under the new law if new circumstances had arisen. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.constitutional_validity_writ: A party has brought a writ proceeding to challenge the constitutional validity of a law.
predicates.challenged_law_repealed: The law whose validity is challenged has been repealed.

issues.definition: When a party challenges a law's constitutionality by writ and that law is repealed, the writ is dismissed as infructuous.
